# az-tf-mlz-azure-firewall

A Fortytwo managed landing zone (MLZ) module for Azure Firewall, in AzAPI: the firewall
(`Microsoft.Network/azureFirewalls`), its public IP addresses, its policy, the policy's rule collection
groups and the IP groups the rules use. Each type besides the firewall is a submodule that can also be
called on its own, so a separate rules state can manage `modules/rule_collection_group` and
`modules/ip_group` without planning the firewall.

- **A firewall in a virtual network hub** (`virtual_network`, `AZFW_VNet`), Basic, Standard or Premium. The first IP
  configuration holds the `AzureFirewallSubnet` and a public IP address; further public IP addresses get
  their own configurations. A management IP configuration in `AzureFirewallManagementSubnet` is required
  for Basic and for forced tunnelling. Public IP addresses are created through
  [`az-tf-mlz-public-ip`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-public-ip), or given by ID.
  Removing or renaming a created address takes one apply: the firewall moves to its new set of addresses
  first, and the old address is deleted after (Azure deletes no address in use). Zones are left to Azure
  unless set; changing them replaces the firewall and its created addresses, which then need new names.
  The private IP address, the next hop for routes to the firewall, is an output.
- **Policy rules only.** The firewall uses a policy the module creates with the firewall's tier
  (`firewall_policy`, `modules/firewall_policy`) or an existing one (`firewall_policy_id`). The classic
  rule collections on the firewall itself are not supported.
- **Rules are maps keyed by name** (groups, collections, rules), so adding one never shifts the others.
  Keys of `ip_groups` work wherever an IP group ID is taken. Rule collection groups are written one at a
  time per policy, before the firewall, and the default `retry` covers `AnotherOperationInProgress`.
- **Removing a setting reaches Azure.** Every policy setting and rule field is sent, empty when unset,
  because azapi compares only the keys in the body.
- Lock, role assignments and diagnostic settings on the firewall, and lock and role assignments on the
  policy, as in Azure Verified Modules, through
  [`az-tf-mlz-interfaces`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-interfaces). The policy's lock
  also covers its rule collection groups, which pass their `lock_dependency` to it.
- **Or a firewall in a Virtual WAN hub** (`virtual_hub`, `AZFW_Hub`, a secured hub), Basic, Standard or Premium: Azure assigns its public
  IP addresses (`public_ip_count`), and `modules/routing_intent` sends the hub's Internet and/or private
  traffic through it. The hub belongs to the caller; moving the firewall to another hub replaces it.

```hcl
module "azure_firewall" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-azure-firewall.git?ref=vX.Y.Z"

  name      = "afw-hub-nwe"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/<subscription>/resourceGroups/<resource group>"
  location  = "norwayeast"
  virtual_network = {
    subnet_id = "<AzureFirewallSubnet ID>"
    public_ip = { name = "pip-afw-hub-nwe" }
  }
  firewall_policy = { name = "afwp-hub-nwe", dns = { proxy_enabled = true } }
  rule_collection_groups = {
    platform = {
      priority = 200
      network_rule_collections = {
        dns = {
          priority = 300
          action   = "Allow"
          rules = {
            spokes = { protocols = ["UDP"], source_addresses = ["10.1.0.0/16"], destination_addresses = ["10.0.0.4"], destination_ports = ["53"] }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The examples deploy a Standard firewall in a VNet hub with a policy, an IP group and rules (`default`), and
one in a Virtual WAN hub with routing intent (`virtual_hub`).

## Optional Inputs

The following input variables are optional (have default values):

### <a name="input_autoscale"></a> [autoscale](#input\_autoscale)

Description: (Optional) Prescaling: the capacity units a Standard or Premium firewall scales between, each 2 to 50, equal (fixed capacity) or more than 1 apart; billed per capacity unit hour beyond the two default instances. Azure's autoscaling when null. Basic does not autoscale (Learn, "Azure Firewall prescaling" and "Azure Firewall performance").

Type:

```hcl
object({
    min_capacity = optional(number)
    max_capacity = optional(number)
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_diagnostic_settings"></a> [diagnostic\_settings](#input\_diagnostic\_settings)

Description: A map of diagnostic settings to create on the resource. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the diagnostic setting. One will be generated if not set, however this will not be unique if you want to create multiple diagnostic setting resources.
- `logs` - (Optional) A set of log entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of a specific log category to enable. Mutually exclusive with `category_group`.
  - `category_group` - (Optional) The name of a log category group to enable (for example, `allLogs` or `audit`). Mutually exclusive with `category`.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the log entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the log entry.
    - `days` - (Optional) The retention period in days. Defaults to `0` (retain indefinitely).
    - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the retention policy is enabled. Defaults to `false`.
- `metrics` - (Optional) A set of metric entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of the metric category to enable.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the metric entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the metric entry, with the same `days` and `enabled` attributes as `logs.retention_policy`.
- `log_analytics_destination_type` - (Optional) The destination type for the diagnostic setting. Possible values are `Dedicated` and `AzureDiagnostics`. Defaults to `Dedicated`.
- `workspace_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the log analytics workspace to send logs and metrics to.
- `storage_account_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the storage account to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_authorization_rule_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the event hub authorization rule to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_name` - (Optional) The name of the event hub. If none is specified, the default event hub will be selected.
- `marketplace_partner_resource_id` - (Optional) The full ARM resource ID of the Marketplace resource to which you would like to send Diagnostic Logs.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name = optional(string, null)
    logs = optional(set(object({
      category       = optional(string, null)
      category_group = optional(string, null)
      enabled        = optional(bool, true)
      retention_policy = optional(object({
        days    = optional(number, 0)
        enabled = optional(bool, false)
      }), {})
    })), [])
    metrics = optional(set(object({
      category = optional(string, null)
      enabled  = optional(bool, true)
      retention_policy = optional(object({
        days    = optional(number, 0)
        enabled = optional(bool, false)
      }), {})
    })), [])
    log_analytics_destination_type           = optional(string, "Dedicated")
    workspace_resource_id                    = optional(string, null)
    storage_account_resource_id              = optional(string, null)
    event_hub_authorization_rule_resource_id = optional(string, null)
    event_hub_name                           = optional(string, null)
    marketplace_partner_resource_id          = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_ignore_body_changes"></a> [ignore\_body\_changes](#input\_ignore\_body\_changes)

Description: Paths in each resource's `body` whose changes the AzAPI provider ignores. Prefer Terraform's `lifecycle.ignore_changes` when the paths are static; use this variable when the paths must be derived from variables or other non-static values.

Paths use dot notation, for example `properties.autoscaleConfiguration`. Individual list items cannot be targeted; ignore the whole list property instead. Configuration changes at an ignored path are **not** sent to Azure until that path is removed from the list. Changes take effect only after an apply, because the value is held in provider-private state.

### <a name="input_role_assignments"></a> [role\_assignments](#input\_role\_assignments)

Description: A map of role assignments to create on the firewall. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the role assignment. If not set, a random UUID will be generated. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
- `role_definition_id_or_name` - The ID or name of the role definition to assign to the principal.
- `principal_id` - The ID of the principal to assign the role to.
- `description` - (Optional) The description of the role assignment.
- `skip_service_principal_aad_check` - (Optional) If set to true, skips the Azure Active Directory check for the service principal in the tenant. Defaults to false.
- `condition` - (Optional) The condition which will be used to scope the role assignment.
- `condition_version` - (Optional) The version of the condition syntax. Leave as `null` if you are not using a condition, if you are then valid values are '2.0'.
- `delegated_managed_identity_resource_id` - (Optional) The delegated Azure Resource Id which contains a Managed Identity. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. This field is only used in cross-tenant scenario.
- `principal_type` - (Optional) The type of the `principal_id`. Possible values are `User`, `Group` and `ServicePrincipal`. It is necessary to explicitly set this attribute when creating role assignments if the principal creating the assignment is constrained by ABAC rules that filters on the PrincipalType attribute.

> Note: only set `skip_service_principal_aad_check` to true if you are assigning a role to a service principal.

Type:

```hcl

    name                                   = optional(string, null)
    role_definition_id_or_name             = string
    principal_id                           = string
    description                            = optional(string, null)
    skip_service_principal_aad_check       = optional(bool, false)
    condition                              = optional(string, null)
    condition_version                      = optional(string, null)
    delegated_managed_identity_resource_id = optional(string, null)
    principal_type                         = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_sku_tier"></a> [sku\_tier](#input\_sku\_tier)

Description: Tier of the firewall and of the policy the module creates: `Basic`, `Standard` or `Premium`. Standard and Premium change into each other in place; changing to or from Basic replaces the firewall (Azure supports no SKU change on a Basic firewall). A policy can't serve a firewall of a lower tier, so when the module creates the policy, give it a new name in the same change: the policy of the new tier is created first and the old one deleted last. While that change applies, the old policy's rule collection groups are deleted before the firewall switches, so plan it for a maintenance window.

Type: `string`

Default: `"Standard"`

### <a name="input_virtual_hub"></a> [virtual\_hub](#input\_virtual\_hub)

Description: (Optional) The firewall in a Virtual WAN hub (`AZFW_Hub`, a secured hub); exactly one of `virtual_network` and `virtual_hub`. The hub belongs to the caller (the Virtual WAN composition creates it).

- `virtual_hub_id` - Resource ID of the virtual hub. Changing it replaces the firewall.
- `public_ip_count` - (Optional) How many public IP addresses Azure assigns to the firewall, 1 to 80 (Microsoft Learn: more can block updates to the firewall and its policy). Defaults to `1`.
- `routing_intent` - (Optional) The hub's routing intent, through `modules/routing_intent`, with this firewall as the next hop: `internet_traffic` (policy `InternetTraffic`) and `private_traffic` (policy `PrivateTrafficPolicy`), both `true` by default, and `name` (defaults to `RoutingIntent`). It is replaced together with the firewall, including when the firewall is renamed or moved to another resource group or region, so that it never names a firewall being deleted. A hub has one routing intent; leave this null when another state manages it.

A firewall in a Virtual WAN hub can be Basic, Standard or Premium (a Basic hub firewall was created in the sandbox on 2026-10-29; Learn's PowerShell tutorial names only Standard and Premium).

Type:

```hcl
object({
    virtual_hub_id  = string
    public_ip_count = optional(number, 1)
    routing_intent = optional(object({
      name             = optional(string, "RoutingIntent")
      internet_traffic = optional(bool, true)
      private_traffic  = optional(bool, true)
    }))
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_virtual_network"></a> [virtual\_network](#input\_virtual\_network)

Description: (Optional) The firewall in a virtual network hub (`AZFW_VNet`); exactly one of `virtual_network` and `virtual_hub`. The subnets belong to the caller (the hub composition creates them). Each public IP address is either created by this module through `az-tf-mlz-public-ip` (a `public_ip` object: `name`, and optionally `public_ip_prefix_id` to take it from a prefix) or an existing one (a `public_ip_resource_id`). Which addresses are created depends only on which objects are set, so names and IDs may be unknown until apply.

- `subnet_id` - Resource ID of the `AzureFirewallSubnet` (/26 or larger).
- `ip_configuration_name` - (Optional) Name of the first IP configuration, which holds the subnet. Defaults to `ipconfig`.
- `public_ip` or `public_ip_resource_id` - (Optional) The first IP configuration's public IP address, created or existing. Neither only with `management` (forced tunnelling without a data-path public IP).
- `additional_public_ips` and `additional_public_ip_resource_ids` - (Optional) Further public IP addresses, created or existing, each its own IP configuration named by its key.
- `management` - (Optional) The management IP configuration, required for Basic and for forced tunnelling: `subnet_id` of the `AzureFirewallManagementSubnet` (/26 or larger), `ip_configuration_name` (defaults to `management`), and exactly one of `public_ip` and `public_ip_resource_id`. Adding or removing it replaces the firewall: Azure enables the management NIC on an existing firewall only by stopping and starting it.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    subnet_id             = string
    ip_configuration_name = optional(string, "ipconfig")
    public_ip = optional(object({
      name                = string
      public_ip_prefix_id = optional(string)
    }))
    public_ip_resource_id = optional(string)
    additional_public_ips = optional(map(object({
      name                = string
      public_ip_prefix_id = optional(string)
    })), {})
    additional_public_ip_resource_ids = optional(map(string), {})
    management = optional(object({
      subnet_id             = string
      ip_configuration_name = optional(string, "management")
      public_ip = optional(object({
        name                = string
        public_ip_prefix_id = optional(string)
      }))
      public_ip_resource_id = optional(string)
    }))
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_zones"></a> [zones](#input\_zones)

Description: (Optional) Availability zones of the firewall and of the public IP addresses the module creates, for example `["1", "2", "3"]`. Null leaves them out, which Microsoft advises for new firewalls: Azure spreads them across zones itself where the region supports it (Azure Firewall FAQ), and the public IP addresses are zone-redundant where the region has zones. Changing them replaces the firewall and the public IP addresses it creates, which then need new names: a removed or replaced address is deleted only after the firewall has moved to its new set.

Type: `list(string)`

Default: `null`

## Outputs

The following outputs are exported:

### <a name="output_firewall_policy_resource_id"></a> [firewall\_policy\_resource\_id](#output\_firewall\_policy\_resource\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the firewall's policy, created by the module or given.

### <a name="output_hub_public_ip_addresses"></a> [hub\_public\_ip\_addresses](#output\_hub\_public\_ip\_addresses)

Description: The public IP addresses Azure assigns to a firewall in a Virtual WAN hub; empty in a VNet hub.

### <a name="output_ip_group_resource_ids"></a> [ip\_group\_resource\_ids](#output\_ip\_group\_resource\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of the IP groups the module creates, by key.

### <a name="output_name"></a> [name](#output\_name)

Description: Name of the firewall.

### <a name="output_private_ip_address"></a> [private\_ip\_address](#output\_private\_ip\_address)

Description: Private IP address of the firewall, the next hop for routes to it: in `AzureFirewallSubnet` for a VNet hub, in the hub's address space for a Virtual WAN hub.

### <a name="output_public_ip_address_ids"></a> [public\_ip\_address\_ids](#output\_public\_ip\_address\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of the firewall's public IP addresses in a VNet hub, created or given, by IP configuration name (the management one included); empty in a Virtual WAN hub.

### <a name="output_public_ip_addresses"></a> [public\_ip\_addresses](#output\_public\_ip\_addresses)

Description: IP addresses of the public IP addresses the module creates, by IP configuration name.

### <a name="output_resource_id"></a> [resource\_id](#output\_resource\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the firewall.

### <a name="output_routing_intent_resource_id"></a> [routing\_intent\_resource\_id](#output\_routing\_intent\_resource\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the hub's routing intent, when the module manages it; otherwise null.

### <a name="output_rule_collection_group_resource_ids"></a> [rule\_collection\_group\_resource\_ids](#output\_rule\_collection\_group\_resource\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of the rule collection groups, by name.

## Development

Tools: Terraform 1.17.0, TFLint 0.65.0, terraform-docs 0.24.0 (the versions CI uses).

| What | Command |
|---|---|
| Format, validate, lint, unit tests, README drift (what CI runs) | `scripts/check.sh` |
| Format the code and regenerate the READMEs first | `scripts/check.sh --fix` |
| Integration tests in Azure | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/integration.sh [dir ...]` |
| Examples: apply, plan again (must be empty), destroy | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/e2e.sh [examples/<name> ...]` |

`README.md` files are generated from `_header.md`, the code and `_footer.md`; do not edit them by hand.

## Versions and releases

Every release is a SemVer tag `vX.Y.Z`; tags never move, and `main` is never consumed. Pin a release:

```hcl
source = "git::https://github.com/fortytwoservices/<repository>.git?ref=vX.Y.Z"
```

Pull requests are squash-merged, and their titles follow Conventional Commits, which set the next
version: `fix:` a patch, `feat:` a minor (a patch before 1.0.0), `feat!:` or `fix!:` a major (a minor
before 1.0.0). `docs:`, `test:`, `ci:`, `chore:` and `refactor:` release nothing. release-please keeps a
release pull request open; merging it writes `CHANGELOG.md`, the tag and the GitHub release.
